title: Building a Culture of Gender Equality
what_it_is: Building a Culture of Gender Equality

sections.label: Singapore women's development milestones
sections.summary: Lists milestones including the 1961 Women's Charter, 1995 CEDAW accession, and the 2022 White Paper on Singapore Women's Development.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since then, other significant milestones include enactment of the Women's Charter in 1961; establishment of the Singapore Council of Women's Organisations in 1980; accession to the United Nations Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women in 1995; launch of the Conversations on Singapore Women's Development initiative in 2020; Year of Celebrating SG Women in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More recently, the 2022 release of the White Paper on Singapore Women's Development outlines Singapore's commitment to a fair, equitable and inclusive society for all women.

sections.label: Men's views and masculinity
sections.summary: States 57% of Singaporean men echoed a sentiment versus 29% of women, and warns of hyper masculinity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Interestingly, but probably not surprisingly, 57% of Singaporean men echoed this sentiment, in contrast to 29% of women." Mr Speaker, failure to respectfully and effectively engage with men and boys can also lead to a climate a culture of hyper or alpha masculinity, and dangerous notions of what it is to be a man.

sections.label: Male suicides and masculinity
sections.summary: Samaritans of Singapore data shows 476 suicides in 2022, 317 or over 66% men, and links patriarchal masculinity to violence.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Data from the Samaritans of Singapore shows that in 2022 there were 476 deaths by suicide, of which 317, or just over 66%, were men.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Men who ascribe to patriarchal notions of masculinity are more likely to be hostile or violent towards women, both at home and in the community.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This, in turn, will have a positive impact on Government and community spending on health, policing and associated welfare services.

sections.label: Men in caring roles
sections.summary: Says men want caring roles but are constrained, stay-home dads increased, and no push exists for men in female professions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand that many may find this an odd suggestion, as it often quite often accurately said that men hold too much power and that they can sometimes use this power to the disadvantage of women.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is despite the 2023 State of the World's Fathers report that showed that both men and women want care to be central to their lives.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These results suggest that men do want to play an active caring role as husbands, fathers and sons, yet are constrained from doing so.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While in Singapore the number of stay-home dads has increased, we need to do more to develop an environment that promotes men adopting caring roles within the family and community, and that such work by men is normal, acceptable and important.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This campaign has slowly and steadily produced positive results, and it is now quite common to see girls and women studying and working in STEM related disciplines.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There has been no similar push, either internationally or here in Singapore, for men to study or work in traditionally female professions, such as nursing, elder care, childcare, secretarial and social work.

sections.label: National Gender Equality Framework
sections.summary: Proposes a National Gender Equality Framework with principles and measurable outcomes to complement existing policy commitments.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A National Gender Equality Framework would articulate a clear roadmap to achieve gender equality across Singapore, underpinned by clear principles and measurable outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A national framework would complement existing policy commitments to women and contain whole-of-Government policy and practice guidance to combat unlawful or dangerous gender norms or stereotypes and empower women and men to achieve their full potential within an inclusive society.

sections.label: Progress for Singapore women
sections.summary: Reports over 95% literacy, three in four women aged 25 to 64 employed, 30% women in Parliament, and top 10 GII ranking.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Our efforts are reflected in the tremendous progress for Singapore women over the years: we have achieved very high literacy rates of over 95%; three out of four women between the ages of 25 and 64 are employed; in Parliament, we have 30% women’s participation, above the international average of about 26%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Singapore was ranked for the first time last year as among top 10 worldwide and first in Asia Pacific for gender equality in the United Nations Human Development Report's Gender Inequality Index (GII).

sections.label: Marriage and Parenthood Survey
sections.summary: In the 2021 Marriage and Parenthood Survey, almost all married respondents agreed fathers and mothers are equally important as caregivers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In the 2021 Marriage and Parenthood Survey, almost all married respondents, men and women, agreed that fathers and mothers are equally important as caregivers for children.

sections.label: Paternity leave doubled
sections.summary: Earlier this year, paternity leave was doubled from two to four weeks, with a message that paternal involvement should be the norm.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, we doubled paternity leave from two to four weeks, with a clear message that we want paternal involvement and that, that should be the norm.

sections.label: Support for caregivers of seniors
sections.summary: The Government is providing additional support to caregivers of seniors, including doubling the Home Caregiving Grant and enhancing the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Government is providing additional support to relieve burden on caregivers of seniors, both men and women through measures such as the doubling of the Home Caregiving Grant, from $200 to $400 a month from 1 March 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The recently announced enhancement to the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme will also help boost the retirement savings of older Singapore Citizens, including caregivers, who have yet to accumulate the current Basic Retirement Sum in their CPF.

sections.label: Workplace fairness and equal opportunities
sections.summary: The passage quotes Prof Razwana and states workplace fairness will be strengthened through the upcoming Workplace Fairness Legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To quote Prof Razwana, "It is a good thing for men, it is a good thing for women and it is a good thing for Singapore." In the workplace, we must do more to facilitate equal opportunities for both men and women.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will strengthen workplace fairness through the upcoming Workplace Fairness Legislation.

sections.label: White Paper on Women's Development
sections.summary: The White Paper on Singapore Women's Development is a 10-year roadmap, with a mid-term review in 2027 and a report to Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The White Paper on Singapore Women’s Development is a 10-year roadmap and a framework to guide our whole-of-society effort; we will undertake a mid-term review in 2027 and report back to Parliament.

sentences.text: Pursuant to Standing Order 2(3)(a), I wish to inform hon Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 12.00 pm, midday.
